### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**2** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **63** of **226** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **163** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **163**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **104** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **10** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7c523aa108650e48d19419ae9b76924c64707741` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `7d1060dbff26c46e814ef582f598f330f0ccf3c1` — the merge of head `7241ddd14f220ed914a01ae9d6be8a6382f82eed` into base `7c523aa108650e48d19419ae9b76924c64707741`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 7d1060dbff26c46e814ef582f598f330f0ccf3c1 && git checkout 7d1060dbff26c46e814ef582f598f330f0ccf3c1
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 7c523aa108650e48d19419ae9b76924c64707741 7241ddd14f220ed914a01ae9d6be8a6382f82eed && git checkout -B drift-repro 7c523aa108650e48d19419ae9b76924c64707741 && git merge --no-ff 7241ddd14f220ed914a01ae9d6be8a6382f82eed

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7c523aa108650e48d19419ae9b76924c64707741
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept-set: unchanged — right.** No door accepts or refuses a request it did not before. `saveMetaItem` (draft and active), `publishMetaItem`, `publishPackageDrafts`, `rollbackMetaItem` and `revertCommit` answer the same requests the same way; only the body two repository writers store from stored material changes.

Both callers, `rollbackMetaItem` and `revertCommit`, reach the live row only through this method.
- **Live-row write of a publish — right.** `promoteDraft` applies the same helper before `deriveActiveBody`; the draft row is still dropped by its own hash, and `expectedDraftHash` still names the stored draft. Both publish doors reach the live row only through this method.
- **One predicate, no new list — right.** The positions removed are the type's redactor's own `notCarriedForwardKeys` (a connector's undeclared `auth` keys and the undeclared keys of an object `retryConfig`), the same answer the save door's carry-forward drains by and the same helper history snapshots already use. Nothing in the diff names a key or a type.
- **Every other body byte for byte — right.** The helper returns the body by reference when the redactor names no position (every type but `connector`, and a connector with nothing undeclared); the two CONTROL pins hold that at the repository and the door.
- **Downstream readers — right.** The registry write-through, the mutation projector, the publish side effects and the mutation event all read `result.item.body`, the body `put` stored, so what the runtime registers after a revert or a publish is what the live row holds.
- **Public surface — right, declared.** No export is added or removed. The exported `SysMetadataRepository`'s `deriveActiveBody` / `deriveRestoredBody` docblocks now say the argument is the stored body without the positions a save drains; the changeset's bullets say the same. `Metadata-protocol: none` is right: what an author can write is unchanged.
- **History rows — right.** Already written through the same helper since #31242; this diff does not touch the history insert.
- **Engine-double ledger — right.** `scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json` gains the three slices the gate pins (`delete`, `findOne`, `update`) for each new fake; both fakes reach the producer-side predicates, and the door file's `find` applies the caller's `limit`.

### ② Semver level

- **`@objectstack/metadata-protocol`: `patch` — right.** A bug fix in a released package; no key, export or accepted value moves. The objectql test file and the pinned ledger publish nothing, so no second changeset is owed.
- **`Clause-②: no` — right.** The diff widens no accept-set and enlarges no public surface, and narrows no published accept-set (the arm's criterion): no door changes what it accepts. The sibling #31242 carried `yes (narrowing)` because it added a published export (`@objectstack/metadata/history-snapshot`) and changed what raw history rows hold; this diff adds no export, so `no` without an arm is consistent with that precedent, and the record is rendered on the narrowing face at the seat's request rather than because the declaration owes it.
- **The hand-back's contract point (publishing a draft that holds an authored undeclared `retryConfig` key now drops it where an active save of that body would keep it) — not a narrowing, not a must-fix; its premise does not hold in the tree.** The save door's spec-conformance check runs on every save, draft mode included (`protocol-save.ts`, `resolveOverlaySchema` → the kernel registry's `connector` entry, `DeclarativeConnectorEntrySchema`); that entry is a closed shape whose authored `retryConfig` is the closed `AuthoredRetryConfigSchema` and whose instance-auth kinds are strict shapes. No door accepts such a key in any mode, so a stored draft holding one is legacy or a direct store write, and an active save of that body is refused rather than kept. Publish writing the body without it is the spec's own refusal made real on stored material — consistent with the published save contract (a save of the served form drains the stored key, and the save names each drop) and with ruling 6677709817 step (c), whose rule the diff extends from the history copy to the live row. The alternative the hand-back offers (draining against the active row) is not needed.
- **Commit revert checked by code reading only — enough.** `revertCommit` calls the same `repo.restoreVersion` with the same `deriveRestoredBody` the per-item rollback uses (`restoreWriteFor`, one derivation for both), and the step sits inside `restoreVersion` before any caller's hook, so no caller can reach the live write around it. Red-first at the repository and the door already shows the method itself.
- **Disclosure — no breach found.** The PR body, the commit message, the changeset and the two source comments stay in product words (which writes drop which positions, where the step sits); the why line is the maintainer's fixed sentence 「QA 第三轮发现的安全加固(细节按披露裁决不公开)」. The test fixtures use labelled placeholder strings; their key names stay at the level the series already publishes on `main`.
- **Check-runs on the head at record time: 30 success, 13 skipped, 3 in progress (Test Core shards 1, 3 and 4), 1 failure.** Every derived gate family that has completed is green: Check Changeset, PR-body guards, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · ESLint, Lint · repo & tooling gates, Lint · CI, release & engine gates (the two engine-double gates), Lint · docs & code guards, Type Check · workspace / source / consumer / debt ledger, Build Core, Test Core shards 2, 6, 7 and 8. The failure is `Test Core (5/8)`: `@objectstack/scenarios` `test/runner/external-driver.test.ts` › "a full crm run through the command: each key reached it in a 0600 file only, and no written artifact holds any" › `Error: Test timed out in 5000ms`. That test drives the scenarios runner over a spawned fake command under vitest's default 5 s budget and imports nothing this diff touches; the diff changes only the connector branch of two repository writers. The merge-base's `Test Core` is green, so the same-signature exception does not apply: the shard is to be re-run and the PR lands only on all green. Judged a timing flake, not a defect of this diff.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Flag: a stored draft with an authored undeclared `retryConfig` key (hand-back "Contract reading").** Answered under ②: the door refuses such a key in every mode, so the case is legacy material and the chosen reading ("a body written from stored material never carries a drained position") stands. No `(narrowing)` arm owed.
- **Flag: `revertCommit` NOT MEASURED.** Answered: covered by construction through the shared `restoreVersion`; code reading is sufficient (see ②).
- **Flag: cross-organization NOT MEASURED.** Answered: the step is a type-level transform of the stored body inside the one write path; it reads no organization, and the repository's row keying is untouched, so there is nothing organization-specific to measure.
- **Flag: other writers listed as out of scope (two of them).** Pre-existing, outside this PR's two methods: escalated, each its own private item. No description here.
- **Flag: legacy rows at rest until the step (b) scrub.** Already ruled (6677709817, (b) after (c)); nothing new for this PR.
- **Open question: test-fake change after the package suites ran.** The door file's `find` now holds the caller's `limit` and matches every stated column; the file was re-run green, and `check:objectql-double-limit` and `check:engine-double-contract` are green on the head. Closed.
- **Author.** The PR is opened by `os-project-manager`, not the fleet bot; the committed commit is signed `Claude` with the session of the drafting thread. Noted for the landing seat.
- **Should-fix (wording, PR body "What changes"):** "the body the protocol's judges see is the body written" is exact for the revert judges and for both derive hooks; the publish door's runtime authoring gate judges the stored draft before the promotion, so for publish the judged body is a superset of the written one (nothing refused less). Reword, or move the step ahead of that gate in a follow-up; no behaviour change owed here.
- **Should-fix (test comment):** in the metadata-protocol test, the comment on the `providerConfig` fixture line ("A DECLARED credential position ... kept in history") describes the wrong class: the headers map is a withheld-whole, carried-forward position, not a declared credential position. Cosmetic.

### ④ Design judgment

After a revert or a publish the live row now holds what every other write already produces for that body. No reader through a declared surface could observe the position before, and no door writes it, so nothing declared is lost — this is an implementation gap closed, not a capability retired at the consumer.
- **Break attempts: 12 shapes tried across every path that writes a live row from stored material (per-item rollback, commit revert, per-item publish, package publish, the derive hooks, the downstream readers, dotted key names, non-object containers, plural type spelling, every other `put` caller in the package, the identical-body skip path, the publish gate's ordering) — none defeats the change.** The one asymmetry found is the publish gate ordering named under ③ (should-fix, wording). Detail is in the private notes.
- **Out-of-scope items from this review:** escalated, each its own private item; not this PR's remainder and not described here.
- **Fail-closed shape kept.** Where the helper cannot remove a named position it throws, as the history insert in `put` already does for the same body on `main`, so the diff adds no new failure mode to a write that succeeded before.
- No must-fix.
